title: Dependency & artifact governance: immutable images, SBOMs, and pinned CUDA/driver stacks for runtime releases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our inference runtime releases have drift across container images, CUDA/driver stacks, and SBOMs. This causes two classes of failures: (1) customer outages when drivers mismatch GPU nodes during rolling upgrades, and (2) hard-to-audit security surface due to missing or inconsistent SBOMs. We need a repeatable, auditable policy for producing immutable container images, attaching SBOM artifacts, and pinning validated CUDA/driver combinations per release channel (edge/latest, stable/LTS).

Goal: Define and deliver a dependency & artifact management workflow that ensures every runtime image published for a release channel has: (A) an immutable image tag and digest, (B) a signed or versioned SBOM stored in the SBOM registry, and (C) an explicit CUDA/driver compatibility entry. Integrate checks into CI, add rollout gates (canary & node-compat checks), and surface the data in the Console release UI and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Every release image built by CI has an immutable tag format and is pushed with digest (registry/release:<channel>-<semver>-<sha>).
Generate SBOM (CycloneDX v1.4 or SPDX v2.3) for every image and upload to s3://redwood-sboms/runtime/<release>/ and link to image metadata.
CI verifies SBOM is present and contains pinned-runtime dependencies and kernel/CUDA driver metadata before allowing release promotion.
Release metadata includes pinned CUDA toolkit and driver versions and a tested compatibility matrix (image -> cudaMajor.minor -> driverVersion).
Rollout gates exist: preflight node-compat check, canary rollout policy, and automated rollback trigger on regressions or node driver mismatch errors.
Console shows SBOM link, image digest, and compatibility note for each release; release notes include upgrade instructions for Dedicated/Private customers.
Automated upgrade tooling can propose upgrade plan for a Dedicated fleet given node driver constraints and image compatibility.
Security review completed and SBOM signing/attestation process documented.
tasks: Design immutable tagging scheme and metadata labels for images
Add SBOM generation step to runtime CI (use Syft + CycloneDX) and upload to SBOM bucket
Create image metadata manifest that includes image digest, SBOM path, tested CUDA toolkits and driver versions
Implement CI gate to prevent promotion if SBOM missing or SBOM scan fails high-severity checks
Add rollout gate: node-compat preflight that queries node driver versions in target cluster
Integrate release metadata into Console release view and release notes generator
Build upgrade planner that suggests node upgrade order given pinned drivers
Document rollback scenarios and add automated rollback trigger in deploy pipeline
decisions: Use immutable tags with <channel>-<semver>-<shortsha> and rely on digests for immutability (trade-off: readable tags vs enforced immutability via digest).
SBOM format: CycloneDX v1.4 as default with SPDX fallback for partners that require it.
SBOM generation tool: Syft in CI (lightweight) and optional Tern scans for deep inspection in nightly security jobs.
Pin CUDA/driver at the release manifest level rather than baking driver into the image to allow smaller image sizes and to respect host-managed drivers on Dedicated/Private deployments.
risks: Pinning drivers reduces flexibility for edge customers who run older nodes. We must provide clear upgrade paths and an upgrade planner.
SBOM generation may expose internal private mappings; access control is required on SBOM bucket.
Automated rollback complexity: partial rollbacks can leave mixed fleet states if not coordinated with node driver upgrades.
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for 2026-02-20 outage where driver mismatch caused canary failures. Initial proposal included driver-baked images; changed to manifest-level pinning to reduce image churn.
2026-03-02 Marco Chen: Implemented initial Syft step in CI pipeline (branch: ci/sbom-syft). Example SBOM uploaded to s3://redwood-sboms/runtime/ci-test/; need access policy review.
2026-03-05 Lena Ortiz (Security): Quick scan on SBOM reveals 2 dev-only packages accidentally included in runtime layer. Filing follow-up ENG-4831 to remove build-time artifacts from final image.

2026-03-09 Marco Chen: Proof-of-concept for image metadata manifest committed: runtime/ci#meta-manifest. Manifest fields: image_digest, sbom_path, tested_cuda_versions, tested_driver_versions, release_channel. Adding CI gate to check presence of sbom_path and that tested_cuda_versions is non-empty.

2026-03-12 Devon Brooks (Platform): Node-compat preflight script prototype (scripts/node-compat-check) can query k8s node labels for nvidia.com/gpu.driverVersion. We should standardize the node label key and include in dedicated deployment docs.
2026-03-12 Marco Chen: Marking WIP — next steps: (1) add canary rollout hook to check node-compat before scheduling canary pods, (2) surface SBOM links in Console release view (designer: DES-2216).
notes: Implementation should be backwards-compatible: existing images without SBOMs must be allowed to exist in 'legacy' channel for one release cycle, but cannot be promoted to LTS.
We will publish an upgrade guide for Dedicated and Private customers that describes how to check node driver versions and how to coordinate cluster node upgrades with image rollout.
Consider adding attestations from our CI signer for SBOMs in a follow-up (ENG-4920).
